name: Trusted CI

# Only ci.yml selects this route. Local calls use the exact caller commit;
# ordinary copied-ref reporting binds this file to protected main as well.
on:
  workflow_call:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  trusted_linux:
    name: CI (Linux Rust 1.98.0)
    runs-on: linux-amd64-cpu8
    timeout-minutes: 75
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: 1.98.0
      RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Rust 1.98.0
        uses: actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@166cdcfd11aee3cb47222f9ddb555ce30ddb9659 # v1.17.0
        with:
          cache: false
          components: clippy,rustfmt
          toolchain: 1.98.0

      - name: Install Rust validation tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@9114bf4d891761788c546334fd37538eae1bf8b3 # v2.87.16
        with:
          checksum: true
          fallback: none
          tool: cargo-audit@0.22.2,cargo-deny@0.20.2,cargo-machete@0.9.2

      - name: Verify exact dependency-policy tools
        run: |
          cargo-audit --version | grep -Fx 'cargo-audit 0.22.2'
          cargo-deny --version | grep -Fx 'cargo-deny 0.20.2'
        shell: bash

      - name: Install Markdown validator
        # Refresh this immutable pin frequently to keep pace with rumdl releases.
        # This section would benefit by a change to the action allowlist
        uses: rvben/rumdl@95a982d941d00cf41a0dcef4d0788bd15a29be1b # v0.2.54
        with:
          install-only: true
          version: "0.2.75"

      - name: Cache trusted Rust inputs
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          cache-bin: false
          cache-targets: false
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: Test exact trusted tool pins
        run: |
          .github/scripts/check-trusted-tool-pins.sh
          .github/scripts/test-trusted-tool-pins.sh

      # `cargo xtask check` runs Markdown, Protobuf, formatting, workspace-version,
      # package-content, compile, Clippy, test, downstream, unused-dependency,
      # dependency-policy, and audit checks. Coverage, profiling, Wasm, and release
      # operations are separate; protected workflow and shell policy run below.
      - name: Run provider-neutral CI
        run: cargo xtask check

      - name: Test protected reporter policy
        env:
          PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: "1"
        run: >-
          python3 -m unittest discover
          -s .github/scripts -p 'test_report_required_ci.py'

      - name: Test anonymous pull-request binding
        env:
          PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: "1"
        run: >-
          python3 -m unittest discover
          -s .github/scripts -p 'test_bind_candidate_pr.py'

      - name: Test credential-free candidate materialization
        run: .github/scripts/test-materialize-candidate.sh

      - name: Test release pull-request path inventory
        run: .github/scripts/test-check-release-pull-request.sh

      - name: Test local release source attachment
        run: |
          .github/scripts/test-attach-release-source.sh
          .github/scripts/test-bind-release-invocation.sh

      - name: Lint GitHub Actions workflows
        uses: devops-actions/actionlint@ec02b36684b2f574f1d219ad0a43b082e46bf3e4 # v0.1.13 (actionlint v1.7.12)

      - name: Lint shell scripts
        uses: ludeeus/action-shellcheck@00cae500b08a931fb5698e11e79bfbd38e612a38 # 2.0.0
        with:
          check_together: true
          scandir: .github/scripts
          version: v0.11.0

  msrv:
    name: CI (Linux Rust 1.95.0)
    runs-on: linux-amd64-cpu8
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: 1.95.0
      RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Rust 1.95.0
        uses: actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@166cdcfd11aee3cb47222f9ddb555ce30ddb9659 # v1.17.0
        with:
          cache: false
          components: clippy
          toolchain: 1.95.0

      - name: Check public workspace at the MSRV
        run: cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace --all-targets --all-features

      - name: Test public workspace at the MSRV
        run: cargo +1.95.0 test --workspace --all-features

  advisory:
    name: CI (${{ matrix.name }}, advisory)
    continue-on-error: true
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 75
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: 1.98.0
      RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: macOS
            runner: macos-latest
          - name: Windows
            runner: windows-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Remove unused preinstalled Homebrew source
        if: ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' }}
        run: .github/scripts/remove-preinstalled-aws-tap.sh

      - name: Set up Rust 1.98.0
        uses: actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@166cdcfd11aee3cb47222f9ddb555ce30ddb9659 # v1.17.0
        with:
          cache: false
          toolchain: 1.98.0

      - name: Restore Rust inputs without saving
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          cache-bin: false
          cache-targets: false
          save-if: false

      # GitHub-hosted advisory lanes cover public workspace portability only.
      # Source-package and release policy remain authoritative on Linux.
      - name: Check public workspace
        run: cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features

      - name: Test public workspace
        run: cargo test --workspace --all-features


  trusted_result:
    name: Linux result
    if: ${{ always() }}
    needs:
      - trusted_linux
      - msrv
    runs-on: linux-amd64-cpu4
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions: {}
    steps:
      # This isolated aggregate consumes only GitHub job results. Missing,
      # skipped, cancelled, or failed authoritative lanes cannot pass staging.
      - name: Require every authoritative Linux lane
        env:
          TRUSTED_LINUX_RESULT: ${{ needs.trusted_linux.result }}
          MSRV_RESULT: ${{ needs.msrv.result }}
        run: |
          test "${TRUSTED_LINUX_RESULT}" = success
          test "${MSRV_RESULT}" = success

name: Required CI reporter

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows:
      - CI
    types:
      - completed

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: required-ci-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  report:
    name: Report reviewed CI
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' &&
      (startsWith(github.event.workflow_run.head_branch, 'pull-request/') ||
       startsWith(github.event.workflow_run.head_branch, 'ci-testing/pr-'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    environment: protected-automation
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      # Load the reporter from protected default-branch policy without checking
      # out or executing any candidate-controlled source.
      - name: Load protected reporter
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          POLICY_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          install -d "${RUNNER_TEMP}/required-ci"
          gh api \
            "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/contents/.github/scripts/report_required_ci.py?ref=${POLICY_SHA}" \
            --jq .content | base64 --decode > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/required-ci/reporter.py"
          test -s "${RUNNER_TEMP}/required-ci/reporter.py"
          python3 -m py_compile "${RUNNER_TEMP}/required-ci/reporter.py"

      - name: Inspect exact-base reviewed result
        id: inspect
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: >-
          python3 "${RUNNER_TEMP}/required-ci/reporter.py" inspect
          --event "${GITHUB_EVENT_PATH}"
          --repository "NVIDIA/yaml-sigil-rs"
          --policy-sha "${GITHUB_SHA}"
          --workflow-id "333755871"
          --workflow-path ".github/workflows/ci.yml"
          --workflow-policy-path ".github/workflows/ci-trusted.yml"
          --workflow-policy-path ".github/workflows/ci-candidate.yml"
          --job-name "Candidate CI / Candidate CI (Linux)"
          --staging-job-name "Trusted CI / Linux result"
          --app-slug "nvidia-yamlsigil-release-pr"

      # Mint only a checks token scoped to this repository after the complete
      # read-only binding succeeds.
      - name: Create repository-scoped check token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.YAML_SIGIL_RELEASE_PR_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.YAML_SIGIL_RELEASE_PR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: NVIDIA
          repositories: yaml-sigil-rs
          permission-checks: write

      # Re-read every live binding immediately before the existing App creates
      # the sole protected required-check verdict.
      - name: Create exact-base required check
        env:
          APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          APP_SLUG: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.app-slug }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: >-
          python3 "${RUNNER_TEMP}/required-ci/reporter.py" report
          --event "${GITHUB_EVENT_PATH}"
          --repository "NVIDIA/yaml-sigil-rs"
          --policy-sha "${GITHUB_SHA}"
          --workflow-id "333755871"
          --workflow-path ".github/workflows/ci.yml"
          --workflow-policy-path ".github/workflows/ci-trusted.yml"
          --workflow-policy-path ".github/workflows/ci-candidate.yml"
          --job-name "Candidate CI / Candidate CI (Linux)"
          --staging-job-name "Trusted CI / Linux result"
          --app-slug "nvidia-yamlsigil-release-pr"

name: Candidate CI

# Only ci.yml selects this route. Local calls use the exact caller commit;
# ordinary copied-ref reporting binds this file to protected main as well.
on:
  workflow_call:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  candidate_binding:
    name: Bind candidate to protected policy and base
    runs-on: linux-amd64-cpu4
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions: {}
    outputs:
      base_ref: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.base_ref }}
      base_sha: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.base_sha }}
      policy_sha: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.policy_sha }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ""
      GITHUB_TOKEN: ""
      GIT_ASKPASS: /bin/false
      GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: /dev/null
      GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: "1"
      GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM: /dev/null
      GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: "0"
      PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: "1"
    steps:
      # Bind the run before any candidate-executable job starts. Downstream
      # jobs rebind these exact objects before materializing contributor code.
      - name: Initialize fresh binding state
        run: install -d -m 0700 "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-binding"

      - name: Stage binder from protected current main
        id: policy
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git init --quiet --initial-branch=main .
          git remote add origin \
            "${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git -c credential.helper= -c http.extraHeader= \
            fetch --quiet --no-tags --no-recurse-submodules --depth=1 \
            origin "+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main"
          policy_sha="$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main)"
          git show \
            "${policy_sha}:.github/scripts/bind-candidate-pr.py" \
            > bind-candidate-pr.py
          chmod 0500 bind-candidate-pr.py
          python3 -m py_compile bind-candidate-pr.py
          printf 'policy_sha=%s\n' "${policy_sha}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-binding

      - name: Bind copied ref to exact policy and contribution base
        id: pull
        env:
          POLICY_SHA: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.policy_sha }}
        run: >-
          python3 ./bind-candidate-pr.py
          --repository "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          --copied-ref "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          --head-sha "${GITHUB_SHA}"
          --policy-sha "${POLICY_SHA}"
          --output "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-binding

  candidate_stable:
    name: Candidate CI (Linux Rust 1.98.0)
    needs:
      - candidate_binding
    runs-on: linux-amd64-cpu8
    timeout-minutes: 75
    permissions: {}
    env:
      ACTIONS_CACHE_URL: ""
      ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN: ""
      ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL: ""
      ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL: ""
      ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN: ""
      CARGO_REGISTRIES_CRATES_IO_TOKEN: ""
      CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WRAPPER: ""
      CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER: ""
      GH_TOKEN: ""
      GITHUB_TOKEN: ""
      GIT_ASKPASS: /bin/false
      GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: /dev/null
      GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: "1"
      GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM: /dev/null
      GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE: "1"
      GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: "0"
      RUSTC_WRAPPER: ""
      RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER: ""
      RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: 1.98.0
      RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings
    steps:
      - name: Prepare fresh candidate state
        run: |
          install -d \
            "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-bootstrap" \
            "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-source" \
            "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-target" \
            "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tmp" \
            "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools" \
            "${RUNNER_TEMP}/cargo-home"
          {
            echo "CARGO_HOME=${RUNNER_TEMP}/cargo-home"
            echo "CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-target"
            echo "TEMP=${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tmp"
            echo "TMP=${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tmp"
            echo "TMPDIR=${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tmp"
          } >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"

      - name: Set up Rust 1.98.0 before candidate materialization
        uses: actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@166cdcfd11aee3cb47222f9ddb555ce30ddb9659 # v1.17.0
        with:
          cache: false
          components: clippy,rustfmt
          toolchain: 1.98.0

      - name: Install validation tools before candidate materialization
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@9114bf4d891761788c546334fd37538eae1bf8b3 # v2.87.16
        with:
          checksum: true
          fallback: none
          tool: cargo-audit@0.22.2,cargo-deny@0.20.2,cargo-machete@0.9.2,shellcheck@0.11.0

      - name: Install Markdown validator before candidate materialization
        # Refresh this immutable pin frequently to keep pace with rumdl releases.
        # This section would benefit by a change to the action allowlist
        uses: rvben/rumdl@95a982d941d00cf41a0dcef4d0788bd15a29be1b # v0.2.54
        with:
          install-only: true
          version: "0.2.75"

      # Stage all executable candidate policy from protected current main with
      # anonymous Git before any candidate-controlled path is materialized.
      - name: Stage protected current-main candidate policy
        id: policy
        run: |
          install -d "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-policy"
          git init --quiet
          git remote add origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git -c credential.helper= fetch --quiet --no-tags --depth=1 origin \
            "+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main"
          policy_sha="$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main)"
          for path in \
            .github/scripts/bind-candidate-pr.py \
            .github/scripts/check-pull-request-commits.sh \
            .github/scripts/check-release-pull-request.sh \
            .github/scripts/install-actionlint.sh \
            .github/scripts/materialize-candidate.sh; do
            destination="${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-policy/${path##*/}"
            git show "${policy_sha}:${path}" > "${destination}"
            chmod 0500 "${destination}"
            test -s "${destination}"
          done
          echo "policy_sha=${policy_sha}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-bootstrap

      - name: Bind copied ref to the live pull request anonymously
        id: pull
        env:
          POLICY_SHA: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.policy_sha }}
        run: >-
          python3 "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-policy/bind-candidate-pr.py"
          --repository "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          --copied-ref "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          --head-sha "${GITHUB_SHA}"
          --policy-sha "${POLICY_SHA}"
          --output "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"

      # The aggregate verdict records the binding established before any
      # candidate job began. Fail if protected policy or the base moved.
      - name: Match pre-execution policy and base binding
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.base_ref }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.base_sha }}
          EXPECTED_BASE_REF: ${{ needs.candidate_binding.outputs.base_ref }}
          EXPECTED_BASE_SHA: ${{ needs.candidate_binding.outputs.base_sha }}
          EXPECTED_POLICY_SHA: ${{ needs.candidate_binding.outputs.policy_sha }}
          POLICY_SHA: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.policy_sha }}
        run: |
          test "${POLICY_SHA}" = "${EXPECTED_POLICY_SHA}"
          test "${BASE_REF}" = "${EXPECTED_BASE_REF}"
          test "${BASE_SHA}" = "${EXPECTED_BASE_SHA}"

      - name: Install actionlint before candidate materialization
        run: >-
          "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-policy/install-actionlint.sh"
          "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-actionlint"

      - name: Freeze fixed candidate validator paths
        id: tools
        run: |
          cargo_source="$(command -v cargo)"
          cargo_bin="${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/$(basename "${cargo_source}")"
          install -m 0500 "${cargo_source}" "${cargo_bin}"
          install -m 0500 "$(command -v cargo-audit)" \
            "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/cargo-audit"
          install -m 0500 "$(command -v cargo-deny)" \
            "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/cargo-deny"
          install -m 0500 "$(command -v cargo-machete)" \
            "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/cargo-machete"
          install -m 0500 "$(command -v rumdl)" \
            "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/rumdl"
          install -m 0500 "$(command -v shellcheck)" \
            "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/shellcheck"
          test -x "${cargo_bin}"
          "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/cargo-audit" --version \
            | grep -Fx 'cargo-audit 0.22.2'
          "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/cargo-deny" --version \
            | grep -Fx 'cargo-deny 0.20.2'
          echo "cargo=${cargo_bin}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          echo "path=${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" \
            >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"

      - name: Materialize exact credential-free candidate
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.base_ref }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.base_sha }}
          COPIED_REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          POLICY_SHA: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.policy_sha }}
        run: >-
          "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-policy/materialize-candidate.sh"
          "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" "${HEAD_SHA}" "${COPIED_REF}"
          "${POLICY_SHA}" "${BASE_REF}" "${BASE_SHA}"
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-source

      - name: Verify exact pull-request base is present
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.base_sha }}
        run: git cat-file -e "${BASE_SHA}^{commit}"
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-source

      - name: Check commit and release-PR policy
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.base_ref }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.base_sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          YAML_SIGIL_RELEASE_PR_BRANCH: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.release_branch }}
          YAML_SIGIL_PROMOTION_BRANCH: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.promotion_branch }}
        run: |
          "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-policy/check-pull-request-commits.sh"
          "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-policy/check-release-pull-request.sh"
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-source

      - name: Lint GitHub Actions workflows
        run: '"${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-actionlint/actionlint"'
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-source

      - name: Lint candidate shell scripts
        run: '"${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/shellcheck" .github/scripts/*.sh'
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-source

      - name: Lint candidate Markdown
        run: '"${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/rumdl" check .'
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-source

      # Resolve the ignored root lockfile before candidate code can execute so
      # dependency-policy tools all inspect one exact submitted graph.
      - name: Resolve candidate dependencies without executing code
        env:
          CARGO_BIN: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.cargo }}
          PATH: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.path }}
        run: '"${CARGO_BIN}" generate-lockfile --manifest-path Cargo.toml'
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-source

      - name: Check candidate dependency use
        env:
          CARGO: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.cargo }}
          PATH: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.path }}
        run: '"${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/cargo-machete" --with-metadata'
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-source

      - name: Check candidate dependency policy
        env:
          CARGO: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.cargo }}
          PATH: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.path }}
        run: |
          "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/cargo-deny" \
            check bans licenses sources -D warnings
          "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/cargo-deny" \
            --manifest-path xtask/Cargo.toml --locked \
            check bans licenses sources -D warnings \
            -A unnecessary-skip -A unmatched-skip
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-source

      - name: Audit candidate dependencies
        env:
          CARGO: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.cargo }}
          PATH: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.path }}
        run: |
          "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/cargo-audit" audit --file Cargo.lock
          "${RUNNER_TEMP}/candidate-tools/cargo-audit" \
            audit --file xtask/Cargo.lock
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-source

      # Candidate execution is terminal. The full workspace audit below is
      # candidate execution rather than trusted pre-execution policy evidence.
      # `check` runs Markdown, Protobuf, formatting, workspace-version,
      # package-content, compile, Clippy, test, downstream, unused-dependency,
      # dependency-policy, and audit checks; optional reports and Wasm are separate.
      # No cache-save, artifact, environment, token, or consumer follows it.
      - name: Run exact candidate
        env:
          CARGO_BIN: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.cargo }}
          PATH: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.path }}
          RELEASE_BRANCH: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.release_branch }}
          RELEASE_BASE_REF: ${{ steps.pull.outputs.base_ref }}
        run: |
          # Only a binder-validated canonical branch enters release-source
          # validation; ordinary candidates skip this release-specific command.
          if [[ -n "${RELEASE_BRANCH}" ]]; then
            # Dependency inspection created this ignored root lockfile. Remove
            # only that regular, untracked file before release-source validation.
            test -f Cargo.lock
            test ! -L Cargo.lock
            test -z "$(git ls-files -- Cargo.lock)"
            rm -- Cargo.lock
            release_version="${RELEASE_BRANCH#release-plz-manual-}"
            "${CARGO_BIN}" run --locked --manifest-path xtask/Cargo.toml -- \
              release check --base-ref "${RELEASE_BASE_REF}" --version "${release_version}"
          fi
          "${CARGO_BIN}" run --locked --manifest-path xtask/Cargo.toml -- check
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/candidate-source

  candidate_msrv:

"""Deterministic trust-boundary tests for the checkout-free Python reporter.

The fixtures model bounded GitHub REST responses and verify the automatic
candidate binding, DCO policy, repository-specific bases and check identity, App scope,
idempotency, and fail-closed behavior. They perform no network access or
repository mutation and are not a second workflow-policy implementation.
"""

assert SPEC is not None and SPEC.loader is not None
reporter = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)

class FakeApi:
    """Deterministic path-keyed API fixture."""

    def __init__(self, responses: dict[tuple[str, str], Any]) -> None:
        """Copy fixtures so each negative case mutates isolated evidence."""

        self.responses = copy.deepcopy(responses)
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, str, Any]] = []

    def get(self, path: str) -> Any:
        """Return the fixture for one read-only REST request."""

        return self._take("GET", path, None)

    def post(self, path: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
        """Return the fixture for one recorded REST mutation."""

        return self._take("POST", path, payload)

    def _take(self, method: str, path: str, payload: Any) -> Any:
        """Record one call and fail if the test did not authorize its path."""

        self.calls.append((method, path, copy.deepcopy(payload)))
        key = (method, path)
        if key not in self.responses:
            raise AssertionError(f"unexpected API call: {method} {path}")
        value = self.responses[key]
        return copy.deepcopy(value)

def staged_fixture() -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[tuple[str, str], Any]]:
    """Model a reviewed writer push of changed workflow bytes without a checkout."""

    event, responses = fixture()
    run = responses[RUN_PATH]
    run["head_branch"] = STAGING_REF
    run["actor"] = copy.deepcopy(STAGING_ACTOR)
    # A rerunner is not the original actor whose exact-head admission matters.
    run["triggering_actor"] = {"id": 99, "login": "rerunner", "type": "User"}
    event["workflow_run"] = copy.deepcopy(run)
    responses[PERMISSION_PATH] = {
        "permission": "write", "user": copy.deepcopy(STAGING_ACTOR)
    }
    responses[COMMITS_PATH][0]["parents"] = [{"sha": POLICY_SHA}]
    ref = responses.pop(("GET", f"{PREFIX}/git/ref/heads/pull-request/{PULL}"))
    ref["ref"] = f"refs/heads/{STAGING_REF}"
    responses[STAGED_REF_PATH] = ref
    responses[JOBS_PATH]["jobs"][0]["name"] = STAGING_JOB
    # Staging is explicitly allowed to test reviewed workflow changes. Any
    # attempt to read/interpret those workflow bytes is an unexpected API call.
    for sha in (POLICY_SHA, HEAD):
        del responses[("GET", f"{PREFIX}/contents/.github/workflows/ci.yml?ref={sha}")]
    return event, responses


def bind_staged(event: dict[str, Any], responses: dict[tuple[str, str], Any]) -> Any:
    """Run the separate staging route under protected enabled policy."""

    return reporter.bind_candidate(
        FakeApi(responses), event, replace(policy(), staging_job_name=STAGING_JOB)
    )

# Documentation

These instructions supplement the repository-root
[`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) for work under `docs/`.

Keep implementation guides aligned with the code and tests in the same
change. Check the following triggers even when the implementation change
does not directly edit a Markdown file.

## Update triggers

| Document | Update when |
|----------|-------------|
| [`yaml-facade.md`](./yaml-facade.md) | Signature-document parsing, canonical serialization, the public Serde representation, the YAML facade example, or its consumer tests change. |
| [`protobuf-facade.md`](./protobuf-facade.md) | Public protobuf facade operations, wire interoperability, the Prost example dependency or message declarations, or the core-only consumer tests change. |
| [`crypto-providers.md`](./crypto-providers.md) | Public crypto types, adapter contracts, qualified or unqualified behavior, async semantics, key binding, error mapping, resource admission, integration examples, qualification call counts, operation costs, or regression coverage change. Update its three-path checklist with the evidence and remaining integrator responsibilities. |
| [`conformance-validation.md`](./conformance-validation.md) | Fixtures, fixture mappings, expected outcomes, ignored tests, advertised profiles, specification imports, attribution-only imports, public APIs exercised by conformance, or deliberate divergences change. Name the affected paths, expected outcomes, and divergence reasons. |
| [`yaml-backend-evaluation.md`](./yaml-backend-evaluation.md) | The current YAML backend, configuration, parser budgets, public Serde boundary, or interoperability evidence changes. Update the sections describing the current implementation and validation. Preserve historical evaluations as dated findings; label corrections or new evaluations explicitly. |

For a new guide, add its update triggers here and link it from the relevant
README or existing guide. For a removed or renamed guide, update this table
and incoming links in the same change. Keep README indexes and summaries
short; link to the guide that owns the detailed explanation.

## Evidence and scope

Distinguish runtime enforcement, repository regression tests, and claims an
integrator must establish for its own adapter or deployment. Keep tested and
untested behavior explicit. A finite qualification suite is narrower evidence
than complete conformance, and an optional whole-artifact limit is operational
policy. Neither changes the specification's requirements.

Name the owning crate or external contract when describing an API. Keep
public API examples synchronized with compiling rustdoc or executable example
coverage. Follow [`examples/AGENTS.md`](../examples/AGENTS.md) when changing
runnable examples and their index.

Prefer each implementation crate's `v1alpha1` namespace in guides. Explain
that default paths name the same definitions and that specification versions
are separate from crate SemVer. For bindings, document the generated
JavaScript namespace as well as the Rust surface and keep examples aligned
with the generated-API tests.

Run the repository Markdown check for documentation changes. When prose
claims a runtime behavior or test outcome changed, run the corresponding
focused tests and the repository's required validation. Keep historical
results and current evidence distinguishable.
